web_blocks.title: 0.1 What Lowe's Does & Our Independent Dual Verdict

web_blocks.html: Lowe's Companies, Inc. (NYSE: LOW) is the second-largest home improvement retailer in the United States. It operates 1,759 U.S. retail stores (~196 million sq ft; ~89% owned) and a 540+ branch Pro supply network [1, 11, 20]. In 2025, Lowe's acquired Foundation Building Materials (FBM, $8.8B) and Artisan Design Group (ADG, $1.3B) to scale Pro distribution [1, 11]. Audited FY2025 net sales reached $86,286M with $10,153M GAAP operating income (11.77% margin) and $7,651M free cash flow (115% of net income) at 26.1% ROIC [1]. Following Q3 FY2026 results on November 18, 2026, management raised FY2026 sales guidance to ~$92.5B (+0.5% comps) and guided adjusted EPS to ~$12.25 [2, 30].

Our price-blind business audit awards Lowe's a COMPOUNDER_PASS with PASS_WITH_WATCH KPI health. At the November 24, 2026 close of $231.04 ($129.63B market cap), shares trade at 18.17x forward P/E, 16.22x P/FCF (6.17% FCF yield), and a 2.12% dividend yield [31]. That 4.4-turn forward P/E discount to Home Depot (22.60x) supports our $268.00 Base Target ($256.50 probability-weighted EV). However, LOW sits +13.61% above its 50-day SMA in a Downtrend U.S. market (27.8% > 50DMA; 10 distribution days), leaving only 1.19:1 CMP reward-to-risk. Our dual verdict is NOT_HELD (0 shares) and WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT (TIER_2, CORE_ALPHA) at $211.18–$223.49 ($200.00 stop; 1.89:1–2.92:1 R:R). We keep 100% of marginal cash in T-bills until price meets our support zone.

book_paragraphs: Welcome to our institutional monograph on Lowe's Companies, Inc. — America's second-largest home improvement retailer, an S&P 500 Dividend King with over six decades of consecutive dividend hikes, and one of the most misunderstood cash-generation engines in U.S. retail. Over the ten chapters ahead, you and I will walk from Carl Buchan's 1946 North Wilkesboro hardware store all the way to Marvin Ellison's $10.1 billion bet on commercial and residential Pro distribution through Foundation Building Materials and Artisan Design Group.

Here is our bottom-line independent verdict right up front, derived strictly after completing our price-blind business audit and full valuation work. On business quality, Lowe's earns a clear COMPOUNDER_PASS (with PASS_WITH_WATCH on leading KPIs): it owns roughly 89 percent of its 1,759 U.S. store buildings, generated $86.3 billion in audited FY2025 sales (ramping toward $92.5 billion in FY2026), converted 115 percent of GAAP net income into $7.65 billion of free cash flow, and posted 26.1 percent audited return on invested capital. Even in the middle of a multi-year housing turnover freeze, this business prints cash.

Yet great underwriting separates business quality from entry price and market timing. At the November 24, 2026 close of $231.04, Lowe's trades at 18.17 times forward earnings and a 6.17 percent free cash flow yield — a four-and-a-half-turn discount to Home Depot that supports our $268.00 Base Target ($256.50 probability-weighted Expected Value). However, shares have surged 16.56 percent in the past month to sit 13.6 percent above their 50-day moving average inside a Downtrend U.S. equity market (27.8 percent breadth above the 50-day SMA, 10 distribution days), right ahead of a pivotal December 9, 2026 Analyst Conference. Because chasing at $231.04 offers only 1.19-to-1 reward-to-risk against our $200.00 stop, our dual verdict is straightforward: we currently hold zero shares (NOT_HELD), we assign new capital a WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT (Tier 2) rating in the $211.18 to $223.49 support zone (restoring 1.89-to-1 to 2.92-to-1 asymmetry), and we keep 100 percent of reviewed marginal cash safely in short-duration T-bills until the tape meets our price.

Before we dive into the history and store economics, keep one mental model front and center as you read: Lowe's is currently a tale of two timelines. On a one-to-three-month timeline, the stock has already sprinted off its summer lows, diesel inflation and wholesale acquisition dilution are weighing on near-term gross margins, and the broader U.S. stock market is in a Downtrend with weak breadth. On a twelve-to-thirty-six-month timeline, however, Lowe's is quietly paying down its Foundation Building Materials and Artisan Design Group acquisition debt at a pace of more than $3 billion per year while preparing to restart a massive share-repurchase program in mid-2027. Our job as disciplined investors is to align our entry price with the long-term cash-flow engine without overpaying for short-term chart extension.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: How to Read This Dossier
book_callouts.text: Chapters 1 through 6 were written strictly price-blind — no stock quotes, no P/E ratios, no chart lines — so you and I could judge Lowe's store economics, Pro acquisitions, management execution, and debt load on their own merits. Only in Chapters 7 through 9 do we unlock the $231.04 share price, peer multiples, Stage 2 chart, and our final No-FOMO action plan.
